 Deni Avdija (foot) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Due to left foot inflammation, Avdija will miss the second game of Portland’s back-to-back. Scoot Henderson is a potential replacement in the starting lineup, but he hasn’t done enough this season to merit streaming in most leagues.

 Damian Lillard, Sidy Cissoko, Toumani Camara, Jayson Kent and Donovan Clingan will start Tuesday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Deni Avdija (foot) is out for Tuesday’s game, which frees up a spot in the Trail Blazers’ starting lineup. In his 10th appearance over two NBA seasons, Kent will make his first career start. He isn’t worth the risk as a streamer. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija (foot) is questionable for Tuesday’s matchup with the Timberwolves. 
 Avdija is dealing with left foot inflammation and soreness, and his late addition to the injury report doesn’t bode well for his availability. His absence doesn’t provide clear, actionable fantasy advice, as Avdija’s production will be covered with a group effort. 
 Chris Youngblood 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Chris Youngblood (foot) is out for Tuesday’s matchup with the Timberwolves. 
 Youngblood’s availability doesn’t impact the world of fantasy hoops, but Scoot Henderson and Sidy Cissoko could see additional run in his absence. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija led the Trail Blazers with 27 points (11-of-19 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block, three three-pointers and five turnovers in a 106-98 loss to the Timberwolves on Monday. 
 Avdija was productive in the first half of this game, entering the break with a game-high 21 points. However, he was only able to add six points after the break, which wasn’t enough to bring Portland back before he checked out with 7:28 left in the game. Avdija has had a strong season, and he has been red-hot lately, averaging 29.7 points and 3.3 triples over his last three games. They’ll remain in Minnesota for a rematch on Tuesday. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija scored 34 points (11-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, a block and three 3-pointers in the 120-107 win over the Kings. 
 Deni got what he wanted against this Kings defense where he got to the paint at a high level. The Kings had no answer to deal with his strength and athleticism barreling into the paint. No matter what they did, they couldn’t stop him. Deni has been awesome this season and has helped lead the Blazers to a great start to the season. 
 Chris Youngblood 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Chris Youngblood (foot) has been ruled out against the Kings on Friday. 
 Youngblood will miss a second straight game, which should allow Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson to take on a few extra minutes. However, neither should see a dramatic boost in production from Youngblood’s absence. Cissoko is already starting and had 19 points on Wednesday. 
 Sidy Cissoko 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #91 
 Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder. 
 Replacing Scoot Henderson (5/2/2 with one three-pointer) in the starting lineup ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Thunder, Cissoko played well in both victories. The Trail Blazers wing totaled 36 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Portland’s two-game sweep of Oklahoma City. While Cissoko isn’t a must-add player right now, he’s worth watching in deep leagues to see if the last two games were a fluke. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder. 
 One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. That’s great for those who used a top-50 draft pick on Avdija. 
 Chris Youngblood 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Chris Youngblood (foot) has been ruled out against the Thunder on Wednesday. 
 Youngblood exited early from Tuesday’s game and will remain sidelined against OKC. Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson should take on a few extra minutes in this game. 
 Sidy Cissoko 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #91 
 Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder. 
 Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks.

 Towns extended his franchise-record streak of double-doubles to 14 to begin the season, finishing two assists shy of a triple-double. Towns has been one of the best players in fantasy basketball this season, and that shouldn’t change anytime soon.

 Jalen Brunson tallied 31 points (10-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Raptors.
 Brunson and the Knicks extended their win streak over the Raptors to 15 games, with the captain making big plays in crunch time. Brunson’s four-point play with 1:25 remaining broke a 102-all tie and sparked a game-ending 9-0 run. The concern is that he landed on Raptors guard Ja’Kobe Walter’s foot after releasing that shot. Brunson remained in the game and did appear to be bothered by his left ankle. We’ll see if his name shows up on the injury report ahead of Thursday’s game against the Timberwolves.

 Walker Kessler (leg) is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz.
 Kessler is dealing with a sore lower right leg, the reason why he was ruled out of Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. Lakers head coach JJ Redick said he didn’t believe the injury would be long-term, adding that he expects Kessler to play on Wednesday. Sandro Mamukelashvili will have an expanded role with the Lakers’ starting center out, while Kevon Looney could enter the rotation.

 Tuesday’s game will be the second Reaves has missed since injuring his left heel during a November 11 win over the Bucks. The plan is for him to take the court Wednesday to test his heel and see how he feels. Quentin Grimes should remain in the starting lineup for as long as Reaves is out.
